source: When Stubb had departed, Ahab stood for a while leaning over the bulwarks; and then, as had been usual with him of late, calling a sailor of the watch, he sent him below for his ivory stool, and also his pipe. Lighting the pipe at the binnacle lamp and planting the stool on the weather side of the deck, he sat and smoked.

In old Norse times, the thrones of the sea-loving Danish kings were fabricated, saith tradition, of the tusks of the narwhale. How could one look at Ahab then, seated on that tripod of bones, without bethinking him of the royalty it symbolized? For a Khan of the plank, and a king of the sea, and a great lord of Leviathans was Ahab.

Some moments passed, during which the thick vapor came from his mouth in quick and constant puffs, which blew back again into his face. “How now,” he soliloquized at last, withdrawing the tube, “this smoking no longer soothes. Oh, my pipe! hard must it go with me if thy charm be gone! Here have I been unconsciously toiling, not pleasuring—aye, and ignorantly smoking to windward all the while; to windward, and with such nervous whiffs, as if, like the dying whale, my final jets were the strongest and fullest of trouble. What business have I with this pipe? This thing that is meant for sereneness, to send up mild white vapors among mild white hairs, not among torn iron-grey locks like mine. I’ll smoke no more—”
He tossed the still lighted pipe into the sea. The fire hissed in the waves; the same instant the ship shot by the bubble the sinking pipe made. With slouched hat, Ahab lurchingly paced the planks.

modern_en.title: Chapter 30 — The Pipe
paragraphs: When Stubb had gone, Ahab stood for a while leaning over the bulwarks. Then, as had been his habit lately, he called a sailor of the watch and sent him below for his ivory stool, and also his pipe. Lighting the pipe at the binnacle lamp (the lamp by the compass) and planting the stool on the weather side of the deck, he sat and smoked.

In old Norse times, the thrones of the sea-loving Danish kings were made, so tradition says, of the tusks of the narwhal. How could anyone look at Ahab then, seated on that tripod of bones, without thinking of the royalty it symbolized? For Ahab was a Khan of the plank, and a king of the sea, and a great lord of Leviathans.

Some moments passed, during which the thick smoke came from his mouth in quick, constant puffs that blew back into his face. "How now," he said to himself at last, taking the stem from his mouth, "this smoking no longer soothes. Oh, my pipe! Things must be going hard with me if your charm is gone! Here I have been unknowingly toiling, not taking pleasure — aye, and ignorantly smoking to windward all the while; to windward, and with such nervous whiffs, as if, like the dying whale, my final spouts were the strongest and fullest of trouble. What business do I have with this pipe? This thing is meant for serenity, to send up mild white vapors among mild white hairs, not among torn iron-gray locks like mine. I'll smoke no more —"

He tossed the still-lit pipe into the sea. The fire hissed in the waves. At the same instant, the ship shot past the bubble the sinking pipe made. With his hat pulled low, Ahab lurched across the planks.

modern_da.title: Kapitel 30 — Piben
paragraphs: Da Stubb var gået, stod Ahab et stykke tid og lænede sig ud over rælingen. Så, som han i den sidste tid havde for vane, kaldte han på en matros fra vagten og sendte ham ned efter sin elfenbensskammel og sin pibe. Han tændte piben ved nathuslampen (lampen ved kompasset), stillede skamlen på luvsiden af dækket og satte sig og røg.

I gamle nordiske tider var de havelskende danske kongers troner, siger overleveringen, lavet af narhvalstænder. Hvordan kunne man så se på Ahab, siddende på den trefod af ben, uden at tænke på det kongedømme, den betegnede? For Ahab var en khan over planken og en konge over havet og en stor herre over Leviatanerne.

Der gik nogle øjeblikke, mens den tykke røg kom ud af hans mund i hurtige, jævne pust, som blæste tilbage i ansigtet på ham. »Hvad nu,« sagde han til sig selv til sidst og tog piben ud af munden, »denne rygning beroliger mig ikke længere. Åh, min pibe! Det må stå dårligt til med mig, hvis din tryllekraft er væk! Her har jeg uvidende slidt, uden at nyde det — ja, og uvidende røget op mod vinden hele tiden; op mod vinden og med så nervøse drag, som om mine sidste udblæsninger, ligesom den døende hvals, var de stærkeste og fyldigste af uro. Hvad har jeg med den her pibe at gøre? Den er til ro, til at sende milde hvide dampe op blandt milde hvide hår, ikke blandt sønderrevne jerngrå lokker som mine. Jeg ryger ikke mere —«

Han kastede den stadig tændte pibe i havet. Ilden hvæsede i bølgerne. I samme øjeblik skød skibet forbi boblen, som den synkende pibe lavede. Med hatten trukket langt ned over øjnene slingrede Ahab hen over planken.
